title: Direct image, derived limits, and completeness
statement:
Levelwise direct image on tower categories has a total right derived functor

$$
 Rf_*^{\operatorname{Tow}}:
 D(\operatorname{Tow}_{A}(X))
 \longrightarrow D(\operatorname{Tow}_{A}(Y)),
$$

with $\operatorname{ev}_nRf_*^{\operatorname{Tow}}M_\bullet\simeq Rf_*M_n$.
For every $M_\bullet$ the canonical map

$$
 Rf_*\Rlim M_\bullet
 \xrightarrow{\sim}
 \Rlim\bigl(Rf_*^{\operatorname{Tow}}M_\bullet\bigr)
$$

is an isomorphism. Under the two canonical Roos triangles associated with the
derived inverse-limit [def-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-limit] construction, it
is induced by the canonical isomorphisms

$$
 Rf_*R\!\prod_nM_n\xrightarrow{\sim}
 R\!\prod_nRf_*M_n
$$

and their commutation with $(1-s)$. If $K\in D(X_{\Proet},A)$ is derived
$I$-complete, then $Rf_*K$ is derived $I$-complete. For every $n\geq1$, the
projection-formula morphism

$$
 (Rf_*K)\otimes_A^LP_n\longrightarrow Rf_*(K\otimes_A^LP_n)
$$

is a functorial isomorphism

$$
 (Rf_*K)\otimes_A^LP_n
 \xrightarrow{\sim}Rf_*(K\otimes_A^LP_n)=Rf_*K_n,
$$

and these isomorphisms commute with $P_{n+1}\to P_n$. Under them, the
completion map for $Rf_*K$ is the composite

$$
 Rf_*K\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf_*\Rlim K_\bullet
 \xrightarrow{\sim}\Rlim Rf_*^{\operatorname{Tow}}K_\bullet.
$$

The commutation $Rf_*\Rlim\xrightarrow{\sim}\Rlim Rf_*^{\operatorname{Tow}}$
and the completeness of $Rf_*K$ for derived complete $K$ are clauses (1), (3)
and (4) of Stacks Project, Lemma (Tag
[099N](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/099N), Section 61.20, Tag
[099L](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/099L)): the Stacks entry assumes
a Noetherian ring $\Lambda$, an ideal $I\subset\Lambda$ and a morphism of
topoi, and states that $Rf_*$ sends $D_{comp}$ into $D_{comp}$ and that
$Rf_*K=\Rlim Rf_*(K\otimes^L_\Lambda\underline{\Lambda/I^n})$; the form used
here is its tower-level refinement over $T_{\Proet}$, and the finite-level
projection-formula isomorphisms coming from
[lemma-weil-pbc-perfect-projection-formula] are not part of the Stacks
statement.

proof.text: By [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum], $\operatorname{Tow}_A(X)$ is Grothendieck abelian. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-functorial-existence] in this category to obtain a functorial tower resolution $M_\bullet\to J_\bullet$. The additive levelwise direct image induces an exact functor $K(\operatorname{Tow}_A(X))\to D(\operatorname{Tow}_A(Y))$: it commutes with shifts and with the finite direct sums and matrices defining cones in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-total-derived] to this functor. This constructs $Rf_*^{\operatorname{Tow}}$, represented on $M_\bullet$ by $f_*J_\bullet$.

source.place: Proof, first sentence: total derived functor

proof.text: For $n\geq1$, define $L_n(V)_m=V$ for $1\leq m\leq n$ and $L_n(V)_m=0$ for $m>n$, with identity transitions below $n$. A tower map $L_n(V)\to J_\bullet$ is uniquely specified by its component $V\to J_n$, the lower components being its composites with the transitions. Thus $L_n\dashv\operatorname{ev}_n$, and $L_n$ is exact because exactness is levelwise [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. For an acyclic complex $V$, $\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet(V,J_n)=\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet(L_nV,J_\bullet)$ is acyclic; hence $J_n$ is K-injective [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived]. Evaluation also preserves the resolution quasi-isomorphism, so $\operatorname{ev}_n(f_*J_\bullet)=f_*J_n$ represents $Rf_*M_n$ by [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-total-derived]. These identifications commute with every tower transition because all the maps are evaluations of the same strict tower resolution.

source.place: Proof, first sentence: exact evaluation and its comparison

proof.text:
For $H\in D(Y_{\Proet},A)$, the adjunction of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations] and the product universal property of [def-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-limit] give
$\operatorname{Hom}(H,Rf_*R\!\prod_nM_n)=\operatorname{Hom}(Lf^*H,R\!\prod_nM_n)=\prod_n\operatorname{Hom}(Lf^*H,M_n)=\prod_n\operatorname{Hom}(H,Rf_*M_n)$.
Consequently $Rf_*R\!\prod_nM_n$ is the product of the $Rf_*M_n$, and the map with components $Rf_*p_n$ is the canonical natural product isomorphism $\alpha$. This proves the product clause without a new lemma.

Write $t_{n+1,n}:M_{n+1}\to M_n$ for the transitions and $p_n$ for the product projections. The shift satisfies $p_ns=t_{n+1,n}p_{n+1}$ [prop-weil-pbc-roos-triangle]. On the image product the shift $s'$ satisfies $p'_ns'=Rf_*(t_{n+1,n})p'_{n+1}$. Since $p'_n\alpha=Rf_*p_n$, both $s'\alpha$ and $\alpha Rf_*s$ have $n$th component $Rf_*(t_{n+1,n}p_{n+1})$. The product universal property therefore gives $s'\alpha=\alpha Rf_*s$, and additivity gives the same equality for $1-s$.

The comparison in the previous steps induces the canonical comparison of the two Roos cones [prop-weil-pbc-roos-triangle], hence the displayed inverse-limit map. To verify its invertibility and its canonical model, use the tower resolution $J_\bullet$ from step 1. The products are represented by $\prod_nJ_n$ [prop-weil-pbc-derived-product-representation]. This product is K-injective: its Hom complex from an acyclic complex is the product of the acyclic Hom complexes into the $J_n$, and products of abelian groups preserve exactness componentwise. The shifted cone of $1-s$ is also K-injective, since its Hom complex is the shifted cone of a map between these acyclic complexes (the cone has the degreewise split short exact sequence with the target and the shifted source). The coefficient inverse image in [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations] is exact, because its coefficient map is an isomorphism, while [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image] supplies a morphism of sites and [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], clause (3), gives exact inverse image on underlying abelian sheaves. Kernels and cokernels of module sheaves are those of their underlying abelian sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], so this is also exact on modules. Its levelwise extension is exact as well. By the Hom adjunction, $f_*$ and its levelwise extension therefore send K-injective complexes to K-injective complexes. Thus $f_*J_\bullet$ is a K-injective tower representing $Rf_*^{\operatorname{Tow}}M_\bullet$, and its product represents the target product. At the complex level the comparison is the ordinary right-adjoint isomorphism $f_*\prod_nJ_n\cong\prod_nf_*J_n$; its components are the product projections, so it is exactly $\alpha$ of step 3. The functor $f_*$ commutes with the finite direct sums and matrices in the cone formula [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. The equality of step 4 therefore gives an actual isomorphism of shifted cone complexes. By [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-total-derived] these complexes compute the source and target of $Rf_*\Rlim M_\bullet\to\Rlim Rf_*^{\operatorname{Tow}}M_\bullet$. This proves the canonical isomorphism and its compatibility with the Roos triangles.

source.place: Proof, comparison of the two Roos triangles; explicit K-injective cone model

proof.text: For each perfect $P_n$ of [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum], [lemma-weil-pbc-perfect-projection-formula] gives $\pi_n:(Rf_*K)\otimes_A^LP_n\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf_*K_n$. In [def-weil-pbc-projection-formula-map] this map is adjoint to the counit tensored with $Lf^*P_n$. Tensoring that same counit with the quotient map $P_{n+1}\to P_n$ gives the commutative square for $\pi_{n+1}$ and $\pi_n$; tensoring it with $A\to P_n$ also gives compatibility with the reduction maps from $Rf_*K$. Consequently these are isomorphisms of the reduction tower together with its maps from $Rf_*K$. By [prop-weil-pbc-koszul-reconstruction], derived complete $K$ has its completion isomorphism $K\to\Rlim K_\bullet$. Apply $Rf_*$ and then step 5. The resulting isomorphism $Rf_*K\to\Rlim Rf_*^{\operatorname{Tow}}K_\bullet$, identified by the $\pi_n$, is the quotient-tower completion map of $Rf_*K$, because all its components are the reduction maps just checked. The functorial identification of the quotient and Koszul completion maps in [prop-weil-pbc-koszul-reconstruction] and the definition [def-weil-pbc-intrinsic-completion] now show that $Rf_*K$ is derived $I$-complete. This also proves precisely the completion composite in the statement.

source.place: Proof, final sentence: projection formula, coefficient compatibility, completion
